purpose: Torsemide helps your body get rid of extra fluid and salt by making you urinate more often. It is used to treat swelling (edema) caused by heart failure, kidney disease, or liver disease. It can also help lower high blood pressure.
how_it_works: Your kidneys filter your blood and decide what to keep and what to flush out. Torsemide works in a part of your kidneys called the 'loop of Henle' and blocks your kidneys from holding onto salt and water. This causes your body to release that extra fluid through your urine, which reduces swelling and takes some pressure off your heart.
common_side_effects: You may need to urinate more frequently, especially after taking your dose. Other common side effects include dizziness, headache, low blood pressure (feeling lightheaded when you stand up), muscle cramps, and feeling thirsty. Your potassium or other electrolyte levels may also drop, so your doctor may check blood tests regularly.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor if you notice muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness, or very little urination, as these could signal low electrolytes or kidney problems. Be careful driving or standing up quickly since it can cause dizziness. Avoid this medication if you are allergic to sulfa drugs, and let your doctor know all other medications you take since torsemide can interact with many drugs including blood pressure medicines and certain antibiotics.
typical_dosing: For most conditions, the starting dose is 5 to 20 mg taken once daily by mouth, usually in the morning to avoid nighttime bathroom trips. Your doctor may increase your dose depending on how your body responds. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
